# UNK-167 sqlx runtime-query allowlist
#
# This file is the canonical registry of `sqlx::query(...)` /
# `sqlx::query_as(...)` / `sqlx::query_scalar(...)` invocations exempted
# from the compile-time-macro requirement. CI greps for runtime sqlx in
# `backend/src/` and rejects any line not containing a fixed string from
# this file (`grep -v -F -f`).
#
# Adding an entry: include reviewer justification in the PR description
# adding it. The carve-out class must be one of:
#   1. DDL (CREATE/DROP/ALTER TYPE) — schema mutation; macros cannot
#      validate against schema that doesn't exist yet at prepare time.
#   2. Dynamic SQL built from runtime input (rare; flag in review).
#   3. `SELECT set_config(...)` GUC mutation — Postgres session/transaction
#      configuration, not data access; macros cannot validate GUC mutation
#      against schema at prepare time.
#   4. Enum-drift test probes — `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` + cast performed
#      at runtime in tests to detect code-vs-schema enum drift.
#
# Each non-comment line is a substring; if it appears in a `grep -rn`
# output line `path:line:content`, that runtime invocation is allowed.
#
# Two pattern styles are mixed deliberately:
#   - `path:` prefixes act as file-level blankets: every runtime sqlx
#     invocation in that file is exempted. Use only when the entire
#     file's runtime usage falls under one carve-out class. New runtime
#     additions to such files pass the guard silently — review them
#     manually against the documented carve-out classes.
#   - `<SQL substring>` patterns scope the exemption to specific call
#     shapes inside files that mix legitimate macros with carve-outs.

# (1, 2, 3) db.rs file-blanket — RLS context GUC plumbing (class 3: set_config +
# current_setting), migration runner DDL (class 1: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
# _sqlx_migrations, BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK), and dynamic migration SQL (class 2:
# sqlx::raw_sql for embedded migration content)
backend/src/db.rs:

# (1, 4) models/manifestation_format.rs file-blanket — enum-drift detection test (ALTER TYPE + ::manifestation_format probe)
backend/src/models/manifestation_format.rs:

# (1, 4) models/user.rs file-blanket — user_role enum-drift detection test (ALTER TYPE + ::user_role cast probe + role-cast fixture)
backend/src/models/user.rs:

# (1, 4) models/validation_status.rs file-blanket — validation_status enum-drift detection test (ALTER TYPE + ::validation_status cast probe)
backend/src/models/validation_status.rs:

# (1, 4) models/reading_status.rs file-blanket — reading_status enum-drift detection test (ALTER TYPE + ::reading_status cast probe)
backend/src/models/reading_status.rs:

# (1, 4) models/content_rating.rs file-blanket — content_rating enum-drift detection test (ALTER TYPE + ::content_rating cast probe)
backend/src/models/content_rating.rs:

# (3) suggest fuzzy leg — SET LOCAL pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold GUC
# (default 0.6 is too strict for typeahead typos); transaction-scoped
sqlx::query("SET LOCAL pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold = 0.3")

# (2) library filter EXPLAIN test — planner introspection over the literal
# any-of/all-of vocabulary filter SQL plus a pre-EXPLAIN ANALYZE; test-only,
# exact strings (tests.rs mixes legitimate macros, no blanket).
sqlx::query("ANALYZE manifestation_genres, genres, manifestations, works")
sqlx::query(explain_any_of_sql)
sqlx::query(explain_all_of_sql)

# (2) sort-index EXPLAIN test — planner introspection over the literal
# `?sort=-pages` ORDER BY, asserting the DESC NULLS LAST pages index is used
# at scale; test-only, same carve-out shape as the filter EXPLAIN above.
sqlx::query(explain_pages_sql)

# (1, 2) subtitle trigram-index EXPLAIN test — planner introspection over the
# literal `subtitle_contains` filter SQL, asserting the subtitle GIN trigram
# index is the access path (not a full-scan Filter) at scale, plus a
# pre-EXPLAIN ANALYZE; test-only, same carve-out shape as the filter EXPLAIN.
sqlx::query("ANALYZE works, manifestations")
sqlx::query(explain_subtitle_sql)

# (3) subtitle trigram-index EXPLAIN test — SET LOCAL enable_seqscan = off makes
# the guard deterministic (the trigram index vs Seq Scan cost is borderline at
# scale and flips on ANALYZE's sample); the GUC penalizes seq scans without
# forbidding them, so a missing index still fails the guard. Transaction-scoped.
sqlx::query("SET LOCAL enable_seqscan = off")

# (2) seed_library_50k test (routes/library/tests.rs): a static,
# multi-statement operator script (BEGIN/DO guard/bulk INSERT/ANALYZE/
# COMMIT) executed verbatim via raw_sql; a batch is structurally not a
# `query!` candidate. The count probes around it use `query_scalar!`
# macros and need no entry.
sqlx::raw_sql(sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(seed_sql.as_str()))

# (3, 4) test_support.rs file-blanket — set_config('app.system_context', ...) in after_connect callback (class 3) plus role-cast drift fixtures for admin/child/adult (class 4); test-only fixture module
backend/src/test_support.rs:

# (3) services/writeback/queue.rs:~1020 RLS impostor test — exact SQL string match
# (not file-anchored because queue.rs is mostly macro-based business logic; a
# blanket would over-allow future runtime drift in the file).
# (2) services/settings.rs file-blanket — dynamic UPDATE SET built from runtime-variable partial update fields (QueryBuilder)
backend/src/services/settings.rs:

SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', $1, true)
